_provenance: Derived from catalog.example.json -- the redacted copy of a real probe-built catalog -- by cloning its rows onto fresh keys. Every Media/Part/Stream shape is ffprobe-derived from real debrid content; only the multiplicity is synthetic, because a one-item section turns the Shuffle, Play Next, Merge and paging checks into no-ops. The debrid links are the example file's placeholder, so a part read fails at the provider rather than serving bytes: test_all.py covers real reads. Extended again for cycle 13: seasons 21 and 22 with an episode each, so a paged season list can return more than one row past the first page, and a second Media on episode 1004, so the Duplicates filter has a duplicate to find on the leaf, its season and the show. Same method -- existing rows cloned onto fresh keys. And three more episodes in the last season, because a shelf's default cap is six and a five-episode library cannot overflow one. The episodes carry no contentRating of their own, because a real PMS gives an episode its show's and a fixture that stores one on every row cannot show it. Extended for the UI suite's last content skips with three movies built the way build_catalog.py builds a row, from real files in the 1.42.2 reference's library: each ffprobe'd (8.1.2) over the 1.42.2 reference's own part URL and run through mediainfo.build_media, the two matched ones identified by metadata.enrich against the TMDB id the 1.42.2 reference matched and given the 1.42.2 reference's plex:// guid. "Trust No One: The Hunt for the Crypto King" and "Tuesday" are the 1.42.2 reference's Dolby Vision profile 5 rows 967 and 1120, and "Vinaipayan" is the 1.42.2 reference's unmatched local://3763, kept unmatched: a keyed run matches the first movie again, and the checks about an unmatched row need one either way. Their links are the same placeholder.

items.title: The Simpsons
items.summary: Set in Springfield, the average American town, the show focuses on the antics and everyday adventures of the Simpson family; Homer, Marge, Bart, Lisa and Maggie, as well as a virtual cast of thousands. Since the beginning, the series has been a pop culture icon, attracting hundreds of celebrities to guest star. The show has also made name for itself in its fearless satirical take on politics, media and American life in general.
